import Mathlib.Analysis.Complex.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.PathConnected
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Star
import Mathlib.Tactic.NormNum
import Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith
import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring
import Mathlib.Tactic.Positivity
open Set Complex
namespace Cassinian331705
noncomputable section
def slit : Set ℂ := {z | z.im = 0 ∧ 1 ≤ z.re}
def G : Set ℂ := slitᶜ
def y : ℂ := ⟨4,1⟩
def z : ℂ := ⟨2,1/2⟩
def cassinian (U : Set ℂ) (a b : ℂ) : ℝ :=
  sSup ((fun p : ℂ => ‖a-b‖ / (‖a-p‖ * ‖b-p‖)) '' frontier U)
def ball (U : Set ℂ) (a : ℂ) (r : ℝ) : Set ℂ := {b ∈ U | cassinian U a b < r}
lemma slit_closed : IsClosed slit :=
  (isClosed_eq continuous_im continuous_const).inter (isClosed_le continuous_const continuous_re)
lemma G_open : IsOpen G := slit_closed.isOpen_compl
lemma zero_mem : (0:ℂ) ∈ G := by norm_num [G,slit]
lemma star : StarConvex ℝ (0:ℂ) G := by
  intro w hw a b ha hb hab
  simp only [G, mem_compl_iff, slit, mem_ofPred_eq] at *
  simp only [smul_zero, zero_add, Complex.smul_im, Complex.smul_re, smul_eq_mul]
  intro h
  by_cases h0 : b = 0
  · norm_num [h0] at h
  have hi : w.im = 0 := (mul_eq_zero.mp h.1).resolve_left h0
  have ble : b ≤ 1 := by linarith
  have hr0 : 0 ≤ w.re := by nlinarith [h.2]
  have hr : 1 ≤ w.re := by nlinarith [h.2, mul_nonneg (sub_nonneg.mpr ble) hr0]
  exact hw ⟨hi,hr⟩
lemma dense_G : Dense G := by
  intro w
  by_cases hw : w ∈ G
  · exact subset_closure hw
  apply Metric.mem_closure_iff.mpr
  intro e he
  have hm : w ∈ slit := by simpa [G] using hw
  have him : w.im = 0 := hm.1
  refine ⟨w + (e/2:ℝ) * I, ?_, ?_⟩
  · simp [G,slit,him,ne_of_gt (half_pos he)]
  · rw [dist_eq_norm]
    have : w - (w + (e/2:ℝ) * I) = -((e/2:ℝ) * I) := by ring
    rw [this, norm_neg, norm_mul, norm_real, norm_I, mul_one, Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_pos (half_pos he)]
    linarith
lemma frontier_G : frontier G = slit := by
  rw [G_open.frontier_eq, dense_G.closure_eq, G]
  simp
lemma G_connected : IsConnected G := (star.isPathConnected zero_mem).isConnected
lemma polynomial_bound (s : ℝ) (hs : 1 ≤ s) : 68/9 < s^2*((s-4)^2+1) := by
  have hss : 1 ≤ s^2 := by nlinarith
  by_cases h1 : s ≤ 5/4
  · have h : 121/16 ≤ (s-4)^2 := by nlinarith
    nlinarith [mul_nonneg (sub_nonneg.mpr hss) (sq_nonneg (s-4))]
  by_cases h2 : s ≤ 2
  · have h : 4 ≤ (s-4)^2 := by nlinarith
    have hq : 25/16 ≤ s^2 := by nlinarith
    nlinarith [mul_nonneg (sub_nonneg.mpr hq) (sub_nonneg.mpr h)]
  by_cases h3 : s ≤ 3
  · have h : 1 ≤ (s-4)^2 := by nlinarith
    have hq : 4 ≤ s^2 := by nlinarith
    nlinarith [mul_nonneg (sub_nonneg.mpr hq) (sub_nonneg.mpr h)]
  · have hq : 9 ≤ s^2 := by nlinarith
    nlinarith [mul_nonneg (sq_nonneg s) (sq_nonneg (s-4))]
lemma norm_sq (w : ℂ) : ‖w‖^2 = w.re^2 + w.im^2 := by
  rw [Complex.sq_norm, Complex.normSq_apply];ring
lemma ratio_bound_y (p : ℂ) (hp : p ∈ frontier G) :
    ‖(0:ℂ)-y‖ / (‖(0:ℂ)-p‖ * ‖y-p‖) ≤ 3/2 := by
  rw [frontier_G] at hp
  have hpi : p.im = 0 := hp.1
  have hpr : 1 ≤ p.re := hp.2
  have h1 := norm_sq p
  have h2 := norm_sq (y-p)
  have hy := norm_sq y
  simp only [sub_re,sub_im,show y.re = 4 from rfl,show y.im = 1 from rfl,hpi,sub_zero] at h2
  change ‖y‖^2 = 4^2+1^2 at hy
  rw [hpi] at h1
  have hn : 0 ≤ ‖p‖ := norm_nonneg _
  have hm : 0 ≤ ‖y-p‖ := norm_nonneg _
  have hp1 : 0 < ‖p‖ := by nlinarith
  have hp2 : 0 < ‖y-p‖ := by nlinarith [sq_nonneg (4-p.re)]
  have hd : 0 < ‖p‖ * ‖y-p‖ := mul_pos hp1 hp2
  simp only [zero_sub, norm_neg]
  apply (div_le_iff₀ hd).mpr
  have hbound := polynomial_bound p.re hpr
  have heq : (‖p‖ * ‖y-p‖)^2 = p.re^2*((p.re-4)^2+1) := by rw [mul_pow,h1,h2];ring
  nlinarith [norm_nonneg y]
lemma y_mem : y ∈ ball G 0 (7/4) := by
  constructor
  · norm_num [G,slit,y]
  · have hne : ((fun p : ℂ => ‖(0:ℂ)-y‖ / (‖(0:ℂ)-p‖ * ‖y-p‖)) '' frontier G).Nonempty := by
      refine ⟨_, ⟨1, ?_, rfl⟩⟩
      rw [frontier_G]; norm_num [slit]
    have h : cassinian G 0 y ≤ 3/2 := csSup_le hne (by
      rintro q ⟨p,hp,rfl⟩;exact ratio_bound_y p hp)
    change cassinian G 0 y < 7/4
    linarith
lemma bounded_z : BddAbove ((fun p : ℂ => ‖(0:ℂ)-z‖ / (‖(0:ℂ)-p‖ * ‖z-p‖)) '' frontier G) := by
  refine ⟨2*‖z‖, ?_⟩
  rintro q ⟨p,hp,rfl⟩
  rw [frontier_G] at hp
  have hpi : p.im = 0 := hp.1
  have hpr : 1 ≤ p.re := hp.2
  have h1 := norm_sq p
  have h2 := norm_sq (z-p)
  simp only [sub_re,sub_im,show z.re = 2 from rfl,show z.im = 1/2 from rfl,hpi,sub_zero] at h2
  rw [hpi] at h1
  have hn : 0 ≤ ‖p‖ := norm_nonneg _
  have hm : 0 ≤ ‖z-p‖ := norm_nonneg _
  have hn1 : 1 ≤ ‖p‖ := by nlinarith
  have hm1 : 1/2 ≤ ‖z-p‖ := by nlinarith [sq_nonneg (2-p.re)]
  have hd : 0 < ‖p‖*‖z-p‖ := by positivity
  simp only [zero_sub,norm_neg]
  apply (div_le_iff₀ hd).mpr
  have hd1 : 1/2 ≤ ‖p‖*‖z-p‖ := by nlinarith
  nlinarith [mul_nonneg (norm_nonneg z) (sub_nonneg.mpr hd1)]
lemma z_not_mem : z ∉ ball G 0 (7/4) := by
  intro hz
  have hp : (2:ℂ) ∈ frontier G := by rw [frontier_G];norm_num [slit]
  have hs : ‖(0:ℂ)-z‖ / (‖(0:ℂ)-(2:ℂ)‖ * ‖z-2‖) ≤ cassinian G 0 z :=
    le_csSup bounded_z ⟨2,hp,rfl⟩
  have h1 := norm_sq z
  have h2 := norm_sq (z-2)
  change ‖z‖^2 = 2^2+(1/2:ℝ)^2 at h1
  simp only [sub_re,sub_im,show z.re = 2 from rfl,show z.im = 1/2 from rfl] at h2
  norm_num only [Complex.re_ofNat, Complex.im_ofNat, sub_self, sub_zero] at h2
  norm_num at h1 h2
  have h3 : ‖z-2‖ = 1/2 := by nlinarith [norm_nonneg (z-2)]
  simp only [zero_sub,norm_neg] at hs
  norm_num [h3] at hs
  have h4 := hz.2
  change cassinian G 0 z < 7/4 at h4
  nlinarith [norm_nonneg z]
lemma midpoint : (1/2:ℝ) • y = z := by apply Complex.ext <;> norm_num [y,z,Complex.smul_re,Complex.smul_im]
theorem counterexample : IsOpen G ∧ IsConnected G ∧ (0:ℂ) ∈ G ∧
    G ≠ Set.univ ∧ StarConvex ℝ (0:ℂ) G ∧ ¬ StarConvex ℝ (0:ℂ) (ball G 0 (7/4)) := by
  refine ⟨G_open,G_connected,zero_mem,?_,star,?_⟩
  · intro h
    have : (1:ℂ) ∈ G := by rw [h];trivial
    norm_num [G,slit] at this
  · intro h
    have hm := h y_mem (by norm_num : (0:ℝ) ≤ 1/2) (by norm_num : (0:ℝ) ≤ 1/2) (by norm_num : (1/2:ℝ)+1/2=1)
    simp only [smul_zero,zero_add,midpoint] at hm
    exact z_not_mem hm
/-- The compactified boundary point at infinity contributes zero, without changing the supremum. -/
lemma infinity_contribution (U : Set ℂ) (a b : ℂ) (hne : (frontier U).Nonempty)
    (hbd : BddAbove ((fun p : ℂ => ‖a-b‖ / (‖a-p‖ * ‖b-p‖)) '' frontier U)) :
    sSup (insert 0 ((fun p : ℂ => ‖a-b‖ / (‖a-p‖ * ‖b-p‖)) '' frontier U)) = cassinian U a b := by
  let S := ((fun p : ℂ => ‖a-b‖ / (‖a-p‖ * ‖b-p‖)) '' frontier U)
  have hs : S.Nonempty := hne.image _
  have hz : 0 ≤ sSup S := by
    obtain ⟨p,hp⟩ := hne
    exact le_trans (div_nonneg (norm_nonneg _) (mul_nonneg (norm_nonneg _) (norm_nonneg _)))
      (le_csSup hbd ⟨p,hp,rfl⟩)
  change sSup (insert 0 S) = sSup S
  apply le_antisymm
  · apply csSup_le (by simp)
    intro q hq
    rcases hq with rfl | hq
    · exact hz
    · exact le_csSup hbd hq
  · apply csSup_le hs
    intro q hq
    apply le_csSup (hbd.insert 0)
    exact Set.mem_insert_of_mem 0 hq
/-- The conjecture in the Euclidean plane, represented by the complex numbers. -/
def SourceClaim : Prop := ∀ (U : Set ℂ) (a : ℂ) (r : ℝ),
  IsOpen U → IsConnected U → U ≠ univ → a ∈ U → 0 < r →
  StarConvex ℝ a U → StarConvex ℝ a (ball U a r)
theorem source_refutation : ¬ SourceClaim := by
  intro h
  exact counterexample.2.2.2.2.2
    (h G 0 (7/4) G_open G_connected counterexample.2.2.2.1 zero_mem (by norm_num) star)
end
end Cassinian331705

/-- Every finite boundary point is visible along its half-open radial segment. -/
def StrictlyStarlike (a : ℂ) (U : Set ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∀ p ∈ frontier U, ∀ s : ℝ, 0 ≤ s → s < 1 → (1-s) • a + s • p ∈ U
def SourceClaimStrict : Prop := ∀ (U : Set ℂ) (a : ℂ) (r : ℝ),
  IsOpen U → IsConnected U → U ≠ univ → a ∈ U → 0 < r →
  StrictlyStarlike a U → StarConvex ℝ a (ball U a r)

-- Equivalent closed half-plane description avoids absolute-value case splits.
def K : Set ℂ := {p | 1 ≤ p.re ∧ 20*p.im ≤ p.re-1 ∧ -(p.re-1) ≤ 20*p.im}
def U : Set ℂ := Kᶜ
lemma closed_K : IsClosed K := by
  exact (isClosed_le continuous_const continuous_re).inter
    ((isClosed_le (continuous_const.mul continuous_im) (continuous_re.sub continuous_const)).inter
      (isClosed_le (continuous_re.sub continuous_const).neg (continuous_const.mul continuous_im)))

lemma zero_U : (0:ℂ) ∈ U := by norm_num [U,K]
lemma star_U : StarConvex ℝ (0:ℂ) U := by
  intro w hw a b ha hb hab
  simp only [U, mem_compl_iff, K, mem_ofPred_eq] at *
  simp only [smul_zero, zero_add, Complex.smul_im, Complex.smul_re, smul_eq_mul]
  intro h
  have hb1 : b ≤ 1 := by linarith
  have hb0 : 0 < b := by
    by_contra hh
    have he : b = 0 := by linarith
    rw [he] at h
    norm_num at h
  apply hw
  constructor
  · nlinarith [mul_nonneg (sub_nonneg.mpr hb1) (show 0 ≤ w.re by nlinarith [h.1])]
  constructor <;> nlinarith
lemma connected_U : IsConnected U := (star_U.isPathConnected zero_U).isConnected
lemma frontier_subset (p : ℂ) (hp : p ∈ frontier U) :
    1 ≤ p.re ∧ (20*p.im = p.re-1 ∨ 20*p.im = -(p.re-1)) := by
  have hk : p ∈ K := by
    have hh := frontier_subset_closure (s := K)
    rw [U, frontier_compl] at hp
    exact closed_K.closure_eq ▸ hh hp
  have hn : ¬ (20*p.im < p.re-1 ∧ -(p.re-1) < 20*p.im) := by
    intro hh
    have ho : IsOpen {q : ℂ | 20*q.im < q.re-1 ∧ -(q.re-1) < 20*q.im} :=
      (isOpen_lt (continuous_const.mul continuous_im) (continuous_re.sub continuous_const)).inter
        (isOpen_lt (continuous_re.sub continuous_const).neg (continuous_const.mul continuous_im))
    have hi : p ∈ interior K := mem_interior.mpr ⟨_, by
      intro q hq
      exact ⟨by dsimp at hq ⊢; linarith [hq.1,hq.2], le_of_lt hq.1, le_of_lt hq.2⟩, ho, hh⟩
    rw [U,frontier_compl,frontier] at hp
    exact hp.2 hi
  exact ⟨hk.1, by by_contra h; push Not at h; exact hn ⟨lt_of_le_of_ne hk.2.1 h.1, lt_of_le_of_ne hk.2.2 (Ne.symm h.2)⟩⟩
lemma strict_U : StrictlyStarlike 0 U := by

  change ¬ (1 ≤ (s • p).re ∧ 20*(s • p).im ≤ (s • p).re-1 ∧ -((s • p).re-1) ≤ 20*(s • p).im)
  simp only [Complex.smul_re,Complex.smul_im,smul_eq_mul]
  intro h
  rcases hh.2 with he | he <;> nlinarith
lemma boundary (p : ℂ) (hr : 1 ≤ p.re)
    (he : 20*p.im = p.re-1 ∨ 20*p.im = -(p.re-1)) : p ∈ frontier U := by
  have hk : p ∈ K := ⟨hr, by rcases he with h | h <;> constructor <;> linarith⟩
  rw [open_U.frontier_eq]
  refine ⟨?_, by simpa [U] using hk⟩
  apply Metric.mem_closure_iff.mpr
  intro e hepos
  refine ⟨p - (e/2:ℝ), ?_, ?_⟩
  · change ¬ (1 ≤ (p-(e/2:ℝ)).re ∧ 20*(p-(e/2:ℝ)).im ≤ (p-(e/2:ℝ)).re-1 ∧ -((p-(e/2:ℝ)).re-1) ≤ 20*(p-(e/2:ℝ)).im)
    simp only [sub_re,sub_im,ofReal_re,ofReal_im,sub_zero]
    intro h
    rcases he with hh | hh <;> linarith
  · rw [dist_eq_norm]
    have hh : p - (p-(e/2:ℝ)) = (e/2:ℝ) := by ring
    rw [hh, norm_real, Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_pos (half_pos hepos)]
    linarith
lemma proper_U : U ≠ univ := by
  intro h
  have hh : (1:ℂ) ∈ U := by rw [h]; trivial
  norm_num [U,K] at hh
lemma frontier_eq : frontier U = {p | 1 ≤ p.re ∧
    (20*p.im = p.re-1 ∨ 20*p.im = -(p.re-1))} := by
  ext p
  exact ⟨frontier_subset p, fun h => boundary p h.1 h.2⟩
lemma K_abs : K = {p : ℂ | 1 ≤ p.re ∧ |p.im| ≤ (p.re-1)/20} := by
  ext p

  constructor
  · rintro ⟨hr,h1,h2⟩

  · rintro ⟨hr,h1,h2⟩
    exact ⟨hr,by constructor <;> linarith⟩
lemma product_lower (A B L M : ℝ) (hA : L ≤ A) (hB : M ≤ B)
    (hL : 0 ≤ L) (hM : 0 ≤ M) : L*M ≤ A*B := by
  nlinarith [mul_nonneg (sub_nonneg.mpr hA) (sub_nonneg.mpr hB)]
lemma polynomial (s v : ℝ) (hs : 1 ≤ s) (hv : 20*v ≤ s-1) :
    153/25 < (s^2+v^2)*((4-s)^2+(1-v)^2) := by
  have hA : s^2 ≤ s^2+v^2 := by nlinarith [sq_nonneg v]

    have hb : 121/16 ≤ (4-s)^2+(1-v)^2 := by nlinarith [sq_nonneg (1-v)]

    linarith
  by_cases h2 : s ≤ 2

    have hb : 4+(19/20:ℝ)^2 ≤ (4-s)^2+(1-v)^2 := by nlinarith [sq_nonneg (4-s-2),sq_nonneg (1-v-19/20)]

  · have ha : 4 ≤ s^2+v^2 := by nlinarith [sq_nonneg v]
    have hb : 1+(9/10:ℝ)^2 ≤ (4-s)^2+(1-v)^2 := by nlinarith [sq_nonneg (4-s-1),sq_nonneg (1-v-9/10)]
    have hh := product_lower _ _ _ _ ha hb (by norm_num) (by norm_num)
    norm_num at hh ⊢; linarith
  by_cases h4 : s ≤ 4
  · have ha : 9 ≤ s^2+v^2 := by nlinarith [sq_nonneg v]
    have hb : (17/20:ℝ)^2 ≤ (4-s)^2+(1-v)^2 := by nlinarith [sq_nonneg (4-s),sq_nonneg (1-v-17/20)]

    have hb : (4/5:ℝ)^2 ≤ (4-s)^2+(1-v)^2 := by nlinarith [sq_nonneg (4-s),sq_nonneg (1-v-4/5)]

lemma ratio_y (p : ℂ) (hp : p ∈ frontier U) :

    have hh : cassinian U 0 y ≤ 5/3 := csSup_le hn (by rintro q ⟨p,hp,rfl⟩; exact ratio_y p hp)

lemma bounded_z_wedge : BddAbove ((fun p : ℂ => ‖(0:ℂ)-z‖ / (‖(0:ℂ)-p‖ * ‖z-p‖)) '' frontier U) := by
  refine ⟨(5/2)*‖z‖, ?_⟩
  rintro q ⟨p,hp,rfl⟩
  have hf := frontier_subset p hp
  have hv : 20*p.im ≤ p.re-1 := by rcases hf.2 with h | h <;> linarith [hf.1]
  have h1 := norm_sq p
  have h2 := norm_sq (z-p)
  simp only [sub_re,sub_im,show z.re = 2 from rfl,show z.im = 1/2 from rfl] at h2
  have hn1 : 1 ≤ ‖p‖ := by nlinarith [norm_nonneg p,sq_nonneg p.im]

    by_cases hr : p.re ≤ 3

    · nlinarith [norm_nonneg (z-p), sq_nonneg (1/2-p.im)]
  have hd1 : 2/5 ≤ ‖p‖*‖z-p‖ := by nlinarith
  have hd : 0 < ‖p‖*‖z-p‖ := by linarith
  simp only [zero_sub,norm_neg]

lemma z_not_ball : z ∉ ball U 0 (7/4) := by

  have h1 := norm_sq z
  have h2 := norm_sq (z-p)

Status: DRAFT; no priority claim, no accepted campaign credit. The literature gate has material unread bodies (see PRIOR-ART.md). Lean replay does not settle novelty.

The source-only ZIP is also self-contained apart from upstream tools. Safely unpack it into an empty directory, then set SOURCE_ZIP to the absolute path of the original ZIP and invoke its scripts/replay.py with another new child-directory name. The source-only archive includes all Lean files, driver, this document, pins, ordinary proof, raw MathDB line, paper source and PDF builder. The full dossier ZIP includes that source ZIP, the draft PDF, source receipts, frozen review/adjudication copies, audit/build logs and manifests. Neither ZIP includes compiler dependencies or local oleans.

## What PASS means

Cassinian, Wedge and Sanity compile with -j1 -DwarningAsError=true and each passes leanchecker. Audit.lean enumerates local module origins including generated declarations; it prints full types and checks bodies, safety, partial flags and transitive axiom lists. Only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound are permitted. The tested run audited 62 declarations. Both Wedge.ordinary_refutation and Wedge.strict_refutation are literal negations of their displayed universal claims. Strict here refers to the domain's finite-boundary-point property; the ball conclusion being contradicted is ordinary starlikeness.

NegativeMidpoint must fail with a type mismatch when trying to use membership of y as membership of z. NegativeStrictSlit must fail with a type mismatch when trying to use wedge strictness for the slit. These controls assert only rejection of those substitutions, not general logical soundness. Supplementary exact optimizations in the paper are not Lean endpoint claims.

MathDB 331705: one wedge refutes both starlikeness readings

Scope and source. Klén–Mohapatra–Sahoo, arXiv:1511.01298v1, Conjecture 4.7, asks whether every positive-radius Cassinian ball centered at a starlike center in a proper starlike domain is starlike about that center. Its statement imposes no boundedness restriction. The actual cached source text was read. Klén, arXiv:1603.00590, Section 2, defines the stricter meaning by requiring [0,p) ⊂ G for each finite boundary point p. Its actual cached definition was also read. This lane performs implementation and validation, not new literature or priority clearance. All existing review qualifications concerning unread literature and campaign novelty remain for root. Credit remains zero; root alone accepts.

Literal definitions. The original Cassinian.lean was copied byte for byte. In particular, cassinian U a b is the real sSup of the image of the actual mathlib frontier U under p ↦ ‖a-b‖/(‖a-p‖‖b-p‖), and ball U a r = {b ∈ U | cassinian U a b < r}. These are the usual Complex Euclidean norm and domain-restricted strict balls, not a boundary surrogate or a chordal norm. SourceClaim remains literally identical. Wedge.lean adds StrictlyStarlike a U := ∀ p ∈ frontier U, ∀ s, 0 ≤ s → s < 1 → (1-s) • a + s • p ∈ U. SourceClaimStrict has the same universal quantifiers and open, connected, proper, center-membership and positive-radius hypotheses as SourceClaim, with StrictlyStarlike replacing the domain's StarConvex hypothesis. Its conclusion is the same ordinary starlikeness of the ball. Thus even with the stronger domain convention the usual asserted ball conclusion fails. No assertion that a strict-witness hypothesis follows from the ordinary hypothesis is used.

Witness. Write p = u+iv. Set K = {u ≥ 1, 20v ≤ u-1, -(u-1) ≤ 20v} and U = C \ K. The theorem K_abs proves K is exactly the requested closed wedge {u ≥ 1, |v| ≤ (u-1)/20}. K is an intersection of closed half-planes, so U is open. It contains 0 and excludes 1. For w ∈ U, if bw ∈ K with 0 ≤ b ≤ 1, the inequalities imply b > 0 and w ∈ K, a contradiction. Thus U is StarConvex about 0 and path connected, hence connected.

Actual frontier. A frontier point lies in K because K is closed. If both oblique inequalities are strict it belongs to an open subset of K, which contradicts frontier membership. Conversely a point with u ≥ 1 and 20v = ±(u-1) lies in K and is approached from U by subtracting a small positive real number. Hence

    frontier U = {u+iv : u ≥ 1, 20v = u-1 or 20v = -(u-1)}.

This is the union of the rays 1+t(1+i/20) and 1+t(1-i/20), t ≥ 0, with t = u-1. Both directions are proved against mathlib frontier. If p lies on either ray and 0 ≤ s < 1, the corresponding equality and membership of sp in K would imply 1 ≤ s. Consequently [0,p) ⊂ U, proving StrictlyStarlike 0 U. The original slit is separately proved not StrictlyStarlike: p=2 and s=1/2 give the excluded point 1.

Exact estimates, checked with fractions before the analytic Lean estimates. Let y=4+i and z=2+i/2=y/2. Both are in U. Put s=Re p, v=Im p. Every frontier point satisfies s ≥ 1 and 20v ≤ s-1. Squared Euclidean norms give

    (‖p‖‖y-p‖)^2 = (s²+v²)((4-s)²+(1-v)²).

On the successive intervals [1,5/4], [5/4,2], [2,3], [3,4], [4,5], [5,∞), lower bounds for this expression are respectively

    121/16, (25/16)(4+(19/20)²), 4(1+(9/10)²),
    9(17/20)², 16(4/5)², 25.

Each is strictly greater than 153/25. For intervals ending at most 5, use s² for the first factor and the indicated real and imaginary distance bounds for the second; for s ≥ 5, s² ≥ 25 and (4-s)² ≥ 1. All these inequalities are proved by exact nlinarith certificates and the elementary product lower-bound lemma. As ‖y‖²=17, every frontier ratio is ≤5/3. The ratio image is nonempty (p=1) and uniformly bounded, so csSup_le gives c_U(0,y) ≤5/3<7/4. This does not infer a strict supremum bound from pointwise strictness without a uniform margin. The proof does not need or assert the exact optimizing frontier point or the proposed decimal extrema.

For z, every frontier point satisfies ‖p‖ ≥1 and ‖z-p‖ ≥2/5. Indeed if s≤3 then v≤1/10 and the imaginary difference is at least 2/5; if s>3 then the real difference has magnitude greater than 1. The ratios are therefore bounded above by (5/2)‖z‖. This establishes the boundedness prerequisite of le_csSup. The explicit upper-ray point p=2+i/20 gives

    ‖p‖² = 1601/400,  ‖z-p‖ = 9/20,  ‖z‖² = 17/4,
    ratio² = 680000/129681 > 49/16 = (7/4)².

Thus c_U(0,z)>7/4, so z is not in the strict ball. The Lean contradiction uses these exact squared identities, positivity, le_csSup and nlinarith; it does not depend on rounded values. The two ball facts and z=y/2 contradict StarConvex ℝ 0 (ball U 0 (7/4)).

Endpoints. Cassinian331705.Wedge.ordinary_refutation : ¬ Cassinian331705.SourceClaim and Cassinian331705.Wedge.strict_refutation : ¬ Cassinian331705.SourceClaimStrict instantiate their respective universal claims with this SAME U, center 0 and radius 7/4. All geometry, actual frontier, bounds and domain facts are proved in Lean. The plane C represents Euclidean R²; one planar counterexample suffices to refute the source's general assertion for dimensions n ≥2. No all-dimensional transport theorem is claimed.

Infinity convention. The source takes boundaries in the one-point compactification, and the ordinary Euclidean-distance Cassinian contribution of infinity is zero for finite a,b, from the limiting quotient as ‖p‖ tends to infinity. The retained infinity_contribution lemma proves that adjoining zero leaves a nonempty bounded nonnegative ratio supremum unchanged. Sanity.lean instantiates it for the wedge and y; bounded_z_wedge also permits its z instance. This is an insertion-of-zero theorem, not a formal construction of the one-point compactification. No chordal-distance substitution is made.

Validation and trust boundary. See replay-receipt.json and logs. The source-only ZIP contains Lean sources and its hash manifest. scripts/replay.py refuses to reuse a directory, rejects unsafe archive entries, checks every source hash, and strictly recompiles Cassinian, Wedge and Sanity with -j1 -DwarningAsError=true. It runs leanchecker on each and the full Audit.lean enumeration of local declarations by module origin, including generated declarations. The audit records full types, body presence (value? true), safety and partial flags, and transitive axioms; only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound are allowed. NegativeMidpoint and NegativeStrictSlit intentionally fail by type mismatch: they test that the y membership theorem cannot prove midpoint membership and that the wedge strictness theorem cannot prove slit strictness. They do not establish general soundness. Sanity examples check both domain memberships, excluded points, frontier samples, Euclidean norm squares, midpoint, both negations and the infinity convention.

The runner sanitizes Lean's environment, uses only pinned cached upstream oleans plus freshly built local modules, sets two-CPU affinity, CPU 120 s and wall 140 s limits, MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2, and a systemd MemoryMax=6G scope. It samples descendant private RSS; receipts record the peak. The upstream compiler and cached pinned mathlib dependencies are trusted and are not rebuilt. Input trees are hash-bound before and after. No read-only input, shared ledger, git state, remote service, browser, or publication is mutated. No background jobs remain at handback. No bounded-domain optional extension is claimed.

A wedge-complement domain with a nonstarlike Cassinian ball

DRAFT - 1 November 2026. Prepared with AI assistance (Codex); no human authorship or affiliation asserted. No priority claim. MathDB 331705.

Abstract

A thin closed wedge removed from the complex plane gives an open, connected, proper domain U containing 0. It is starlike about 0 both in the segment sense and in the finite-boundary-point strict sense. Nevertheless its strict Cassinian ball of radius 7/4 contains y = 4+i and omits z = y/2. We give rational estimates sufficient for this conclusion and an exact evaluation at y on each of the two boundary rays. Two immutable Lean modules certify the geometric construction and the negations of the universal claims for the two domain hypotheses. The sharper evaluation and motivating slit computation are ordinary mathematical supplements. A bounded literature check found no explicit antecedent in the inspected bodies, but several important bodies remain unavailable; novelty is not established.

1. Definitions and the assertion being tested

Throughout, C is the Euclidean plane with modulus |.|, and a domain is a nonempty connected open subset of C. For a proper domain D and finite a,b in D, define

c_D(a,b) = sup { |a-b| / (|a-p| |b-p|) : p in boundary D },
B_c,D(a,r) = { b in D : c_D(a,b) < r },  r > 0.                         (1)

Boundary means the finite Euclidean frontier. Distances in (1) are Euclidean, not chordal. For the witnesses used below the boundary is nonempty, and the ratio set is bounded. The one-point compactification convention in the source adds infinity to an unbounded domain's boundary. For finite a,b its contribution is 0: the quotient tends to 0 as |p| tends to infinity. Adjoining 0 does not change a nonempty bounded supremum of nonnegative numbers. The formal certificate proves this insertion-of-zero fact, rather than constructing the compactification itself.

A set D containing a is ordinarily starlike about a if (1-t)a+tb belongs to D for every b in D and 0 <= t <= 1. Here 'strictly starlike' means that (1-t)a+tp belongs to D for every finite p in boundary D and 0 <= t < 1. This is the boundary-point convention of [2, Section 2]. Another convention requires boundedness and exactly one boundary intersection on every ray; it is not the convention asserted for our unbounded U. The distinction matters: a slit complement is ordinarily starlike but fails the boundary-point condition.

The assertion in [1, Conjecture 4.7] says: for every proper starlike domain D, every starlike center a in D, and every r > 0, B_c,D(a,r) is starlike about a. We test both the ordinary and the boundary-point strict domain hypothesis, retaining the ordinary conclusion. Failure of the ordinary conclusion also prevents the usual stronger strict conclusion for an open ball. A planar counterexample refutes an assertion posed for all dimensions n >= 2; no transport to every dimension is needed.

2. The wedge and its actual frontier

Put

K = { u+iv : u >= 1, |v| <= (u-1)/20 },       U = C minus K.              (2)

y = 4+i,             z = 2+i/2,              r = 7/4.                  (3)

Theorem. U is an open connected proper domain containing 0. It satisfies both starlikeness conditions of Section 1, but B_c,U(0,7/4) is not starlike about 0.

Proof of the domain assertions. K is the intersection of the three closed half-planes u >= 1, 20v <= u-1 and -20v <= u-1, so U is open. It contains 0 and excludes 1. Suppose w is in U and bw is in K, where 0 <= b <= 1. Then b Re(w) >= 1 implies b > 0. Also

20b |Im(w)| <= b Re(w)-1 <= b(Re(w)-1).

Division by b shows w is in K, a contradiction. Thus [0,w] lies in U. These segments connect each point to 0, proving path connectedness and hence connectedness. Direct substitution shows y,z are in U.

We claim that the finite frontier is exactly

boundary U = { 1+t(1+i/20) : t >= 0 }
             union { 1+t(1-i/20) : t >= 0 }.                            (4)

A frontier point belongs to K since K is closed. If u > 1 and both oblique inequalities are strict, the point is interior to K and cannot be in the frontier. At u = 1 the inequalities force v = 0. The remaining points satisfy u >= 1 and 20v = u-1 or 20v = -(u-1), precisely (4). Conversely, each such point p belongs to K, and p-delta belongs to U for every positive real delta: either its real part is below 1, or an oblique inequality fails. Taking delta down to 0 proves frontier membership. This verifies both inclusions for the actual frontier, rather than substituting a convenient boundary subset.

For strict starlikeness, let p be on a ray in (4) and let 0 <= b < 1. The ray equality gives 20|Im(bp)| = b(Re(p)-1). If bp were in K, it would also give 20|Im(bp)| <= b Re(p)-1, forcing b >= 1. Thus bp belongs to U, including the case p = 1. This proves the finite-boundary-point strict condition.

It remains to show that y belongs to the ball while its midpoint z does not. The next two sections do this with a uniform margin. All domain and frontier arguments above occur in Wedge.lean. In particular, the proof does not rely on a numerical picture of the removed wedge.

4. Excluding the midpoint; the slit limit

For a valid use of a boundary witness in a real supremum, first check boundedness at z. On the frontier, |p| >= 1. If s <= 3, then v <= 1/10, so |z-p| >= |1/2-v| >= 2/5. If s > 3, the real distance |2-s| exceeds 1. Thus all ratios at z are bounded above by (5/2)|z|. The point

p_0 = 2+i/20

lies on the upper ray, with

|p_0|² = 1601/400,      |z-p_0| = 9/20,      |z|² = 17/4.

Its boundary ratio has square

|z|² / (|p_0|² |z-p_0|²) = 680000/129681 > 49/16.                    (8)

The final inequality is the integer inequality 10880000 > 6354369. All quantities are positive, hence the ratio itself exceeds 7/4. Boundedness and the definition of supremum give c_U(0,z) > 7/4. Consequently y belongs to the strict ball and z = y/2 does not. The ordinary starlikeness conclusion fails. Together with Section 2 this proves the theorem under both domain hypotheses.

Slit motivation (ordinary supplement). Let G = C minus [1,infinity). This is the zero-angle version of (2); it is open and ordinarily starlike about 0. Its frontier is [1,infinity). A point 2 of that frontier has midpoint 1 outside G, so G fails the strict boundary-point condition. This explains why a positive wedge angle is useful.

For b = y or z and real p = s >= 1, minimize s² |b-s|². At y the polynomial is s²((s-4)²+1). Its derivative is 2s(2s²-12s+17), with critical points 3 +/- sqrt(2)/2. On [1,infinity), the minimum is 10 at s = 1: the other candidate minimum has value 71/4-2sqrt(2) > 10, since 31 > 8sqrt(2). Thus c_G(0,y) = sqrt(17/10).

At z the polynomial is s²((s-2)²+1/4). Its derivative is s(4s²-12s+17/2); the interior local minimum is at s = (6+sqrt(2))/4. Its value is (71-8sqrt(2))/64, which is less than the endpoint value 5/4 because 71-8sqrt(2) < 80. Therefore

c_G(0,z) = 4sqrt(17)/sqrt(71-8sqrt(2)) > 7/4.                            (9)
